name: SpaceX
day_summary: SPCX is recovering on Juneteenth-eve (Day 5 post-IPO), gravitating toward the June 20 weekly options max pain level of $195 from yesterday's close of $191.82. As of pre-market and early trading, SPCX is estimated near $195.17 — a partial recovery from the FOMC-driven Day 4 selloff. The session is thin: Juneteenth-eve tape (last trading day before June 19 holiday) means institutional desks are reducing book and volumes will be lighter than normal. Two key forces define today: (1) June 20 weekly options max pain at $195 — dealers who sold $195 puts are now long gamma above $195 (stabilizing); (2) Iran ceasefire confirmed in effect — the primary blocking condition for the $190–$200 entry framework is cleared. The entry framework that prior briefs pre-positioned is ACTIVE: $190–$200 zone + Iran signed + Brent below $82 (~$78) = conditions met. The remaining gate is the macro regime (VIX 18.44, SPX barely above 7,460) — justifying a 50% initial position with a put hedge, reserving the other 50% for June 22 (Monday) post-Juneteenth confirmation. NOTE: SPCX data for June 18 has limited reliability given pre-market data conflicts; $195.17 is the best available estimate. This is a morning pre-session brief generated at 11:30 UTC (7:30 AM ET).

decision.rationale: HOLD at low conviction — entry zone ACTIVE, Iranian blocker CLEARED, macro regime STILL ELEVATED. The framework entry conditions are met: $190–$200 zone, Iran ceasefire confirmed, Brent ~$78. The only gate is the macro regime: VIX 18.44 (above 18), SPX at 7,464 (barely above 7,460 floor). The sequence for execution: (1) TODAY (June 18): if SPCX is in the $190–$200 zone at market open, enter 50% of intended position with a $185 June 20 put hedge; accept that today is thin-tape Juneteenth-eve; (2) JUNE 22 (Monday): if VIX is back below 18 AND SPX is recovering toward 7,480–7,500, execute the remaining 50%; (3) STOP: $185 daily close — do not hold through $185 without a hedge. Do NOT add above $200 until VIX <17 and SPX >7,500. The June 20 options expiry at max pain $195 is the near-term anchor — positions inside $195 have the mechanical dealer bid supporting them into Friday's close.
